root_cause.text: The AMD DRM display BIOS parsers (`bios_parser.c` and `bios_parser2.c`) used unbounded `for (;;)` record-chain traversal that relied only on malformed-free VBIOS terminators, so a VBIOS image missing the `0xFF`/zero-size sentinel could make probe-time loops run indefinitely and eventually read past the validated header boundary.
root_cause.evidence: The patch says “All 14 record-chain walk loops in bios_parser.c and bios_parser2.c use for(;;) and only terminate on a 0xFF record_type sentinel or zero record_size,” and it replaces each with `for (i = 0; i < BIOS_MAX_NUM_RECORD; i++)` while adding `#define BIOS_MAX_NUM_RECORD 256` “to prevent unbounded looping if the VBIOS image is malformed and lacks a terminator.”

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly contains the vulnerable unbounded record-chain traversal pattern described in the root cause. Multiple functions use `for (;;)` to walk BIOS record chains by repeatedly doing `offset += header->ucRecordSize;` and only stopping when they see a terminator: for example `bios_parser_get_i2c_info()` breaks only on `if (LAST_RECORD_TYPE == header->ucRecordType || !header->ucRecordSize) break;`, and then advances with `offset += header->ucRecordSize;`. Similar loops appear in `bios_parser_get_gpio_record()`, `bios_parser_get_device_tag_record()`, `get_hpd_record()`, and `get_i2c_record()`. The code does check `if (!header) return ...`, but there is no explicit bound check against the validated table/header end before incrementing across records, and the loop termination still relies on a well-formed `0xff` or zero-size sentinel. Nothing in this function body shows the later fix of bounding traversal to the record table size or otherwise preventing indefinite/overrun traversal, so `has_bug=true` and `is_fixed=false`.
